ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; no refund to rider. No account action on the driver (NS-1 satisfied).
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute entered NS-0 on the driver-cancelled, rider-alleged-no-show branch: the record shows cancelled_by = driver at 09:57:20, 6 min 20 s after acceptance, with a $6.61 cancellation fee on record [F4][F7][NS-0]. The fee therefore stands or falls on NS-1's three conditions, all of which the trace settles as ✓.

NS-1(i): the arrival confirmation was a driver tap, not a platform auto-detection — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:54:15 [F6], and I record it as a driver_tap per the record's own wording [F6][NS-1]. NS-1(ii): at the moment of that tap the driver was 40 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius [F6][F1][NS-1]. NS-1(iii): after the tap the driver stayed continuously within 200 m for 3 min 5 s (185 s) until cancelling, which exceeds the 3-minute default threshold [F6][F2][NS-1]. No record sets a different no-show threshold and no free-wait figure is substituted for it [F4][NS-1]. The trace also confirms the GPS covers the wait without a break, so (iii) is measured, not inferred [F2][F6][NS-1]. The driver's own post-hoc statement that he waited more than 3 minutes [F12] is consistent with, but not needed for, the GPS record, which controls anyway [F3][NS-1].

The driver's two chat messages are consistent with the timeline: an arrival notice at 09:54 and a cancellation notice at 09:57, both timestamped, with a complete two-message record [F9][F10][F11][NS-1]. Nothing in them, in the driver's statement [F12], or in the rider's complaint (that she was charged despite the driver cancelling) shows any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. The complaint is a fee grievance, not a safety report [NS-0][SAFE-1].

Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) are all satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee is validly charged and no refund is due [F6][F7][NS-1]. Since no refund is owed and no RD-1 violation is recorded on this no-show case, RD-6's account-review trigger is not met on the case outcome; the driver's profile (3 disputes, 2 upheld, no-show 2 in 90 d) [F17] cannot itself decide this case, and the trace requires no flag [F17][RD-6]. The rider's profile is likewise not decisive [F16][NS-1].
